pa:2611.11740.name: Creative Priming: Decoupling Process from Product to Escape the Creative Paradox
pa:2611.11740.desc: A method called creative priming uses a priming model trained with GRPO to generate prompt-specific primers that help a response model produce novel, high-quality, and diverse outputs by separating the creative process from response generation.

pa:2611.12875.name: Click3R: Interactive Stereo 3D Reconstruction with Sparse Correspondence Clicks
pa:2611.12875.desc: A framework for interactive geometric correction enables sparse human correspondence clicks to improve feed-forward 3D reconstruction by injecting constraints through a lightweight adapter.

pa:2610.37570.name: LCM-Promo: An LLM-Based Uplift Model for Promotion Allocation
pa:2610.37570.desc: LCM-Promo, a finetuned large language model trained on transactional commerce data, predicts promotion response through monotonic curves and single-token conversion-threshold probabilities, improving conversion and reducing promotion cost in a production A/B test.

pa:2611.12870.name: SWAM: Scaling World Action Models with Cross-Modal Alignment
pa:2611.12870.desc: World action models jointly predict video and actions conditioned on language. pa:2611.01112.name: Auriga Technical Report: A Task-Agnostic Agent Harness for Zero-Shot Embodied Manipulation
pa:2611.01112.desc: Auriga, a task-agnostic agent harness, closes most of the planning-execution gap in zero-shot robot manipulation by combining explicit task beliefs, calibrated 3D measurements, dual-arm control, and execution monitoring, achieving state-of-the-art results on RoboDojo and RoboCasa365.

pa:2611.11994.name: EmoHarness: Boosting Multimodal Emotion Understanding with Meta-Harness Evolving
pa:2611.11994.desc: Small multimodal models can misjudge emotion when words, voice, and visual cues conflict. We present EmoHarness, which runs such a model, the frozen student, inside a harness: the prompts, settings, and verification code around its calls. A human-written starting harness, the scaffold, numbers the student's visual observations, transcript, and prosody descriptions as citable evidence and has the s

pa:2611.11995.desc: In this work, we study whether frontier agent can continually improve real-world AI infrastructure over long horizons. We introduce Infrathon, a benchmark of diverse, long-horizon AI infrastructure optimization tasks across different levels. We evaluate six models across 150 runs with 24-hour budgets, totaling over 10,000 GPU-hours. Our results show that model rankings vary with the evaluation hor
pa:2611.11995.zh: 首度考核AI助理處理複雜系統工程的實力

pa:2611.09501.name: e-means: outperforming k-means (in one-tenth the epochs)
pa:2611.09501.desc: Lloyd's k-means algorithm is a long-running standard for clustering, with applications in data analysis, retrieval, quantization and data curation. In this paper, we introduce an exponential moving average optimization procedure for k-means with mini-batch updates, powered by modern deep learning machinery and new insights. We also establish scaling laws on how decay rate and batch size impact fin

pa:2611.10592.name: MotionGraphicsBench: Evaluating Motion Graphics Generation with Programmatic Verification
pa:2611.10592.desc: Large language models can generate motion graphics from static images and natural language requests, but it remains difficult to evaluate how well models can follow requests that combine spatial, appearance, and temporal requirements. We introduce MotionGraphicsBench, an expert-curated benchmark of 100 instances for animating an input static SVG with a motion edit prompt. By supplying all required

pa:2611.12167.name: FraudBench: A Legal Evaluation of AI Deception
pa:2611.12167.desc: We introduce FraudBench, an evaluation of large language models' (LLMs) propensities to recommend, assist, or directly take actions that would constitute fraud under U.S. law. Our evaluation contains a novel dataset of 159 scenarios based on real-world U.S. court cases and validated by legal experts. pa:2611.07464.name: FINCOSMOS: An Open-World Evaluation Paradigm for Agents in Finance
pa:2611.07464.desc: Language agents increasingly work for users on the open Web, and finance is where trusting them is hardest. The data must come from the Web, the strategy lives in the user's head, and correctness depends on time, so an agent can fail silently: a strategy the user never asked for, unverified data, or a backtest that uses the future yields a report as convincing as a correct one. Existing benchmarks

pa:2611.12527.name: WaveGen: Truly End-to-End Waveform Generation via Internal Spectral Trajectory Learning
pa:2611.12527.desc: WaveGen is a fully end-to-end diffusion framework for text-to-waveform generation that jointly learns spectral and waveform trajectories via Spectral Forcing without external audio codecs, vocoders, latent models, alignment modules, or self-supervised representations, achieving state-of-the-art text-to-speech results.

pa:2611.12934.name: EarthRecord: From Pixels to Land Change with Multimodal Agents over Four Decades of Satellite Imagery
pa:2611.12934.desc: While multimodal agents now carry out complex data analysis with tools, their ability to turn decades of satellite imagery into reliable land-change analysis, crucial for Earth observation science, remains unmeasured. Existing benchmarks fall short: they pose questions on curated images or give agents preprocessed inputs, leaving out the raw multi-sensor archives where such analysis begins. We int

pa:2611.12865.name: Shortcuts and Boundaries: Verifiable RL Misalignment and Contextual Safety Learning
pa:2611.12865.desc: Reinforcement learning agents can exploit verifiable reward-context conflicts to earn higher rewards through noncompliant shortcuts, while contextual penalties and safety learning can improve compliance without sacrificing task capability.

pa:2611.13560.name: Are Dense Rewards Worth Their Tokens in GRPO?
pa:2611.13560.desc: At matched compute, dense process rewards such as Monte-Carlo rewards underperform standard GRPO for language-model reasoning, while selecting prompts with predicted success near 1/2 yields small consistent accuracy gains.

pa:2611.13572.name: Market-Conditioned JEPA: Learning from Unpredictable Market Shocks
pa:2611.13572.desc: A market-conditioned joint-embedding predictive architecture improves financial time-series prediction by conditioning on a leave-one-out market factor, enhancing market exposure, risk, liquidity, and return forecasts.

pa:2611.14210.name: Tree-Ising: Repairing Language Models with Bit-Level Ising Edits
pa:2611.14210.desc: Tree-Ising repairs reasoning loops in LLM weights by solving sparse Ising/QUBO problems over BF16 parameters, improving math benchmark accuracy with fewer weight edits and no gradient or LLM-token cost.
pa:2611.14210.zh: 直接修改AI內部數值來治好鬼打牆
pa:2611.14210.why: 不用重新訓練模型，直接修正內部參數就能解決數學推理卡住的問題，省時又省力

pa:2611.14309.name: MMDM: Measuring Massive Multitask Decision Making
pa:2611.14309.desc: System-1 Decision Models directly make structured probabilistic decisions over query-specified options given a state in a single forward pass, without autoregressively generating reasoning trajectories or textual responses. Recent evaluations cover diverse tasks but often rely on existing benchmarks, where prior exposure to test material can obscure generalization. Moreover, real-world decision ma

pa:2611.13907.name: EVAThink: Evidence Sufficiency-Guided Training for Adaptive Thinking in Video Understanding
pa:2611.13907.desc: EVAThink trains vision-language models to adaptively choose between direct answering and reasoning based on whether sampled video frames provide sufficient evidence, improving video understanding under fixed frame budgets.

pa:2611.12200.name: Learning to Act with World Models by Valuing What Comes Next
pa:2611.12200.desc: WM-PPO combines a world model with PPO’s critic to create auxiliary policy advantages and value targets from predicted successor states, improving task success without privileged information.

pa:2611.11166.name: DexForesight: Grounding Dexterous Policies with Implicit Spatial Foresight
pa:2611.11166.desc: Dexterous manipulation requires rich spatial foresight over both the surrounding scene and the robot hand. Existing world-action models often acquire such predictive knowledge through explicit future prediction. pa:2611.13348.name: ProTEUS: A mutation-resolved world model for closed-loop protein evolution
pa:2611.13348.desc: ProTEUS is a mutation-resolved world model that combines sequence, evolutionary, and structural representations with fast all-atom prediction and closed-loop feedback to guide protein evolution and improve mutant activity.

pa:2611.14488.name: Is Your Robot's Memory Just a Clock? Temporal Shortcuts in Memory-Augmented VLA Policies
pa:2611.14488.desc: Memory in vision-language-action policies can mistake pauses for progress because it is indexed by time, causing early stopping, while event-based indexing mitigates this without retraining.

pa:2611.13482.name: ExRL: Sample-Efficient Online Adaptation of Long-Chunk Policies via Execution Length Control
pa:2611.13482.desc: Execution at the Right Length (ExRL) enables sample-efficient adaptation of long-chunk robot policies by training a lightweight adapter to predict each chunk’s execution length using off-policy reinforcement learning.

pa:2611.03142.name: DepthGraft: Structural Regularization through Hierarchical Cross-Layer KV Reconstruction
pa:2611.03142.desc: DepthGraft improves deep language model training by hierarchically sharing key-value representations across layers, reducing memory use while boosting accuracy.

pa:2611.12426.name: dNaViT: Discrete Codes are General-Purpose Visual Representations
pa:2611.12426.desc: A discrete native-resolution vision transformer with grouped product quantization and a dual-branch objective acts as a versatile visual tokenizer, matching or exceeding task-specific baselines across visual understanding, generation, and editing tasks.

pa:2611.14033.name: Few-Step Streaming Video Generation via Condition Shifting
pa:2611.14033.desc: APEX extends a streaming video generation method by replacing a separate fake-score network with condition shifting to estimate the generated distribution’s velocity field, improving instruction following and visual aesthetics while reducing memory and iteration time relative to DMD.
pa:2611.14033.zh: 只要幾步就能流暢生成影片，畫質更好又省記憶體
pa:2611.14033.why: 不用複雜的額外計算就能更快生成高品質影片，聽指令的能力也更好

pa:2611.12411.name: PhysOPSD: Code as Privilege for Physically Plausible Video Generation
pa:2611.12411.desc: PhysOPSD uses executable code as privileged physical context to improve the physical plausibility of video generative models through on-policy self-distillation with dual-level privilege and controlled variations.

pa:2611.12885.name: World In-Context Learning for Agentic Robot Manipulation
pa:2611.12885.desc: Trained action policies write manipulation skill into network weights, tying what is learned to the distribution it is learned from. In-context learning (ICL) avoids this coupling but has not matched trained policies, because a demonstration recorded in another scene carries no feedback from the world the robot currently faces. We observe that what an agent learns in context is semantic, recording
pa:2611.12885.zh: 突破機器人現場學習瓶頸實現更靈活的操控能力
pa:2611.12885.why: 解決過去機器人換到新環境就呆住的問題，學會看著現場示範就直接模仿操作

pa:2611.12955.name: Predictive Surprise as Self-Grounding Concept Bottleneck for Interpretable Time Series
pa:2611.12955.desc: A self-supervised method segments time series by predictive surprise from a frozen forecaster, clusters segments into dynamical concepts, and classifies with reliability-aware abstention, achieving competitive accuracy and interpretability without annotations.

pa:2611.05927.name: Modality-Aware Expert Pruning for MoE-Based Multimodal Large Language Models
pa:2611.05927.desc: MAEP is a training-free modality-aware expert pruning framework that decomposes expert importance by modality to compress MoE-based multimodal LLMs, reducing memory while maintaining competitive multimodal and text performance.

pa:2611.01527.desc: A scientific agent can give the same verdict while reading and citing different evidence. pa:2611.14516.name: TorchCurves: Differentiable Parametric Curves
pa:2611.14516.desc: TorchCurves is a PyTorch library that enables differentiable, learnable vector-valued parametric curves for integration with neural models and applications such as continuous embeddings, Kolmogorov-Arnold networks, and functional regression.

pa:2611.10866.name: The Surprising Effectiveness of Deleting Weights in LLM Post-Training
pa:2611.10866.desc: How little of a pretrained large language model (LLM) has to change for it to acquire new capabilities? We find that zeroing fewer than 0.05% of its weights, with no other modification, matches full fine-tuning (FFT) at scale across three LLM post-training regimes: reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards, supervised fine-tuning, and on-policy distillation. pa:2611.10015.name: Micius-Flash: Lightweight Agentic Intelligence for Engineering
pa:2611.10015.desc: Micius-Flash is a 27B-parameter multimodal reasoning model trained with a knowledge-tree data pipeline and multi-teacher on-policy distillation, achieving strong hardware and semiconductor agent benchmark results and supporting tool-integrated engineering workflows.

pa:2611.10649.name: MACaQ: Fast, Model Agnostic Calibrated Quantization for Low-Precision Weights and Activations
pa:2611.10649.desc: MACaQ is an MXFP4 W4A4 post-training quantization method that quantizes each linear layer independently using online activation transforms and Hessian-aware refinement, reducing cost while preserving accuracy across language and diffusion models.

pa:2611.12184.name: Blind Variation, Selective Retention: Improving Creative Idea Generation in AI Scientists
pa:2611.12184.desc: Scientific discovery requires ideas that are original, useful, and non-obvious. Yet AI scientists are typically given as much task information as possible during idea generation, which can anchor generation toward familiar approaches. pa:2611.13885.name: Are Causal Neuron Circuits Unique and Transferable?
pa:2611.13885.desc: Interpretability demonstrations often show that intervening on a group of neurons changes a model's answer. A recent example removes an 18-neuron group in Qwen3-32B and the model answers "Simba" instead of "Scar" to a two-hop Lion King riddle. pa:2611.14083.name: Sable: A Small-Field Sumcheck Argument for Bit-Exact Inference of Large Language Models
pa:2611.14083.desc: We present Sable, an argument system and single-GPU prover for the statement that a committed, integer-quantized transformer produced a given token sequence from a given prompt, bit for bit. pa:2611.14320.name: Don't Just Trust Your Memory: Evidence-Linked Memory Reduces Memory-Induced Degradation in LLM Agents
pa:2611.14320.desc: WikiTrace links each distilled lesson to its source trajectory and rationale, enabling LLM agents to verify and correct memories before acting, improving performance and reducing memory-induced degradation across agentic benchmarks.

pa:2611.13995.name: Lipschitz-Controlled Flow Matching for Robust Image Restoration
pa:2611.13995.desc: LipsFlower stabilizes flow-matching image restoration by combining Lipschitz-aware architecture and regularization to reduce perturbation amplification while maintaining competitive restoration quality.

pa:2611.14116.name: Visual Similarity in Adult Word Extension and Artificial Word Learning
pa:2611.14116.desc: Visual similarity measured by a self-supervised visual encoder partially explains word generalization in adults and artificial learners, while the composition of teaching examples contributes additional structure beyond that distance.

pa:2611.13425.name: Prompt2Echo (P2Echo): Text-Prompted Multi-View Echocardiography Segmentation with One Model
pa:2611.13425.desc: P2Echo is a unified view-aware text-prompted segmentation framework that uses dynamic image-text alignment to segment diverse cardiac structures across multiple echocardiographic views with high accuracy and low computational cost.

pa:2611.10486.name: Test-Time Scaling for Diffusion Language Models with Frequency-Aware Remasking
pa:2611.10486.desc: Diffusion language models (DLMs) generate text through iterative denoising, where decisions about which tokens to commit or remask strongly affect output quality. pa:2611.12177.name: Embodied First Exam
pa:2611.12177.desc: Early successes on agentic robotics point to a potential paradigm shift toward using coding agents to control robots. Existing robotics benchmarks are built around visuomotor policy learning, leaving it open whether coding agents can reliably control diverse robots under physical-world constraints. We therefore introduce the Embodied First Exam, a unified, comprehensive, and agent-native evaluatio

pa:2611.14115.name: LEASH: Stay Safe in Agentic Robotics
pa:2611.14115.desc: Foundation models such as GPT and Claude have shown strong capabilities in spatial understanding and embodied intelligence. These advances make agentic robotics a promising path toward artificial general intelligence in robotics. pa:2611.13576.name: PhyRubric: Rubric-Grounded Diagnostic Evaluation of Physical Commonsense in Text-to-Video Generation
pa:2611.13576.desc: A rubric-based diagnostic benchmark and judge assess physical commonsense in text-to-video generation, showing that current models still struggle and that the judge aligns closely with human judgments.

pa:2610.40754.name: DyCraft: An Agentic System for Long-Horizon 4D Scene Generation
pa:2610.40754.desc: DyCraft improves long-horizon 3D animation by decomposing it into planned static scenes, keyframe storyboards, and local motion authoring to reduce physical errors.

pa:2611.11912.name: LO-World: Unified BEV Latent Modeling for Joint 4D Occupancy and LiDAR Forecasting
pa:2611.11912.desc: A unified 4D world model jointly forecasts LiDAR point clouds and 3D semantic occupancy in a shared BEV latent space, improving accuracy and real-time throughput.

pa:2611.13001.name: One Table, Many Queries: Benchmarking Generalist Tabular Models Across Generation, Imputation, and Prediction
pa:2611.13001.desc: A large aligned benchmark reveals that tabular generation, imputation, and prediction share useful conditional information but show distinct fidelity rankings and objective interactions, motivating unified models that improve categorical reconstruction and joint sampling.

pa:2611.14413.name: Bits or permutations? Spending a fixed inference budget on weight precision or on option-order averaging in small local language models
pa:2611.14413.desc: Local language models can save memory by storing weights in fewer bits, and they can reduce sensitivity to the order of answer options by averaging a few reorderings. We ask whether the first makes the second worse, and which is the cheaper way to spend a fixed budget. pa:2611.13843.name: PolyRoute: A Twelve-Language and Code-Mixed Benchmark for Typed-Decision Routing, with Baselines and a Leaderboard
pa:2611.13843.desc: Typed-decision encoders answer a question about a text in one forward pass, but their behaviour outside English is rarely measured on a fixed yardstick. pa:2611.13410.name: SteerDistill: Quantizing LLM Agents via Closed-Loop Teacher Steering
pa:2611.13410.desc: Low-bit quantized LLM agents can recover much of their task success through closed-loop guidance from a full-precision teacher, followed by unassisted student training on corrected and reference turns.

pa:2611.13758.name: Mixed Signals: Weight-Space Programming for EEG and ECG
pa:2611.13758.desc: Weight-space programming allows language models to read a trained neural network's weights and edit them. This opens the door to ``training'' by reasoning rather than through gradient descent. pa:2611.08379.name: Module-Aware Optimization for Graph Neural Networks
pa:2611.08379.desc: GraphMuon adapts Muon's matrix orthogonalization to the covariance of graph-propagated representations, reducing graph-induced update amplification and speeding validation-loss time-to-target on graph benchmarks.

pa:2608.22237.name: Read Less, Solve More: Token-Efficient Sparse Reading of External Content for AI Agents
pa:2608.22237.desc: Web-facing AI agents repeatedly access webpages, documents, repositories, and tool responses, yet reading interfaces often expose entire objects when only sparse evidence is needed. pa:2611.08286.name: Interactive Visual Gym: Evaluating Visual Interaction Models with Simulated Users in Interactive Worlds
pa:2611.08286.desc: Interactive Visual Gym enables closed-loop evaluation and training of visual interaction models by jointly simulating task environments and human users, exposing limitations in state-of-the-art VLMs and improving performance through closed-loop training.

pa:2610.40394.name: Scaling Mathematical Proof Supervision from Structured Textbooks
pa:2610.40394.desc: A large-scale corpus of structured proof-supervision records derived from university mathematics textbooks improves language model mathematical reasoning by 16.7 percentage points over a base model when used for fine-tuning.

pa:2607.24999.name: CogBattery: Human-Referenced Evaluation of Cognitive Task Behavior and Structure in Language Models
pa:2607.24999.desc: CogBattery compares open-weight language models to humans across cognitive tasks, revealing that matching effect directions does not imply human-like error patterns or confidence calibration.

pa:2603.27343.name: WMIP: A Working-Memory-Inspired Programmable Probe of Cumulative State Tracking in Large Language Models
pa:2603.27343.desc: Large language models struggle with cumulative state tracking across multiple updates despite strong single-step arithmetic, and their measured accuracy depends heavily on output protocols.

pa:2611.10193.name: Ensemble Routing for Prompt-Adaptive Cost-Aware LLM Inference
pa:2611.10193.desc: PISA and PISA-E use prompt-adaptive capability estimation to route prompts or select cost-aware ensembles, improving cost-performance trade-offs across LLM routing benchmarks.

pa:2610.39671.name: Incentivizing Self-Learning in Large Language Models via Reinforcement Learning
pa:2610.39671.desc: Large language models (LLMs) draw on parametric knowledge and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to solve knowledge-intensive tasks. pa:2611.18919.name: Correcting Persistent Failures in Point-Cloud Grasping Policies using Human Demonstrations in Virtual Reality
pa:2611.18919.desc: A human-in-the-loop failure-mining pipeline turns persistently unsolved grasps of a reinforcement-learning point-cloud policy into virtual-reality human demonstrations, improving hard-case success without reducing generalization to unseen objects.

pa:2611.16642.name: Dataset Distillation via Drifting
pa:2611.16642.desc: A dataset distillation method learns synthetic samples that approximate per-class data distributions in a feature extractor's latent space, improving distribution coverage and classification training while supporting visualization and other modalities.

pa:2611.21439.name: A Reinforcement Learning Method to Navigate SMEFT Operator Space
pa:2611.21439.desc: A reinforcement learning agent with a lightweight actor-critic architecture explores the Standard Model Effective Field Theory operator space to discover diverse high-quality theory hypotheses and improve global fits.

pa:2611.21072.name: Sage S2.1 Flash Technical Report
pa:2611.21072.desc: We introduce Sage S1.5 Flash, a 320-billion-parameter general-purpose mixture-of-experts model designed to reason over scientific evidence and act in interactive environments. Sage Sci-Perception uses dedicated encoders for molecular graphs and biological sequences and represents spectra as ordered patches of measurements. Modality-specific projectors map these representations into the input space
pa:2611.21072.zh: 能看懂科學數據與分子結構的超大型AI模型
pa:2611.21072.why: 它能直接理解科學實驗數據並在互動環境中推理，比以往模型更擅長處理複雜科學任務

pa:2611.17110.name: SALA: Semantically Aligned Latent Actions Enable Dual-Axis Scaling of Embodied Foundation Models
pa:2611.17110.desc: SALA aligns latent actions across human and robot videos by using language-based semantic similarities to form a shared latent action space that supervises embodied foundation model training and improves robot task performance.

pa:2611.17933.name: OutfitterBench: Evaluating LLM Agents on Long-Horizon Resource Allocation and Commitment Coordination
pa:2611.17933.desc: OutfitterBench evaluates LLM agents managing a 200-day outdoor-equipment rental business under fixed capital and uncertain demand, revealing limitations in sustaining feasible commitments and reallocating resources.

pa:2611.19537.name: Continuation-Guided LLM Evolution of Program Policies and Goal Compilers in Craftax
pa:2611.19537.desc: A framework uses coding agents and a feedback cascade to synthesize code-based policies that achieve long-horizon success and can be factored into a reusable goal compiler for zero-shot transfer to new tasks.

pa:2611.21218.name: InclusionMed: Benchmarking AI for Inclusive Healthcare
pa:2611.21218.desc: InclusionMed is an open medical AI evaluation initiative that audits and reproduces benchmarks across healthcare roles and capabilities, revealing that model rankings and inference costs vary by context and motivating broader, context-specific evaluation.
pa:2611.21218.zh: 全面檢測醫療AI在不同情境下表現的評測系統
pa:2611.21218.why: 揪出醫療AI在不同應用下的真實表現與成本差異，幫助醫療領域挑選最適合的AI工具

pa:2611.20148.name: Centered Ablation: Why Last-Layer Directional Ablation Under-Fires or Collapses, and a Closed-Form Fix
pa:2611.20148.desc: Directional ablation removes a hidden state's component along a "behaviour direction" while a language model runs. It is the standard way to switch a behaviour such as refusal off, but it is erratic: on some models it barely fires, on others the text collapses into repetition. We show why, and fix it. At the last residual stream, ablation is exactly a logit bias: a fixed vocabulary footprint scale

pa:2611.20218.name: SWE-CoWork: Benchmarking Coding Agents as Digital Employees in Organizations
pa:2611.20218.desc: A benchmark of realistic software engineering assignments reveals that current coding agents struggle to track requirements from clarification through implementation, verification, and handoff, completing few tasks despite partial test success.
pa:2611.20218.zh: 測試AI軟體工程師在真實公司環境的協作能力

pa:2611.20385.name: DominoBench: Evaluating Multi-Step Physical Reasoning from Still Images
pa:2611.20385.desc: A new benchmark, DominoBench, shows that current vision-language and multimodal models cannot reliably predict physical outcomes from still images unless the critical calculation and necessary quantities are provided.

pa:2605.09614.name: Reflection Anchors for Propagation-Aware Visual Retention in Long-Chain Multimodal Reasoning
pa:2605.09614.desc: Long chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning improves large vision--language models, but visual information often fades during generation, limiting long-horizon multimodal reasoning. pa:2611.20882.name: Accelerate Bench: Evaluating Agents for Application-Level Program Optimization
pa:2611.20882.desc: Application optimization requires coding agents to discover useful changes and coordinate them across a complete program while preserving the required computation. We introduce Accelerate Bench, a benchmark of 32 CPU optimization tasks adapted from scientific applications and supercomputing competitions. Each task provides a working program and specifies the workload, correctness requirements, tim

pa:2611.18668.name: UMM-JEPA: Generative Pretraining via Masked Next-Scale Representation Prediction for Unified Multimodal Models
pa:2611.18668.desc: Reformulating generation as progressive prediction of continuous perceptual representations improves visual understanding in unified multimodal models more than discrete-code or latent-flow objectives.

pa:2611.20192.name: GlyphAtlas: Disentangling Stroke Detail from Layout for Scene Text Synthesis
pa:2611.20192.desc: GlyphAtlas uses a dedicated glyph atlas and atlas-anchored attention to provide fine-grained stroke references for scene text synthesis, improving stroke accuracy and zero-shot transfer.

pa:2611.21607.name: ScaleVLA: Scaling Vision-Language-Action Models to 552 Billion Parameters
pa:2611.21607.desc: Frontier Vision-Language Models (VLMs) such as GPT-6 Astra have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in robot control, suggesting that broad pretraining provides knowledge valuable for physical action. pa:2611.21339.name: MovieRoll: A Systematic Framework for Rolling Out Long-Form Videos
pa:2611.21339.desc: Streaming video generation must sustain quality beyond the training horizon while handling self-generated history and growing cache costs. To address these challenges, we present MovieRoll, a base-to-distilled framework that connects streaming fine-tuning, long-rollout distillation, and long-horizon inference. We first establish a robust multi-step base through Window-wise Teacher Forcing (WinTF),

pa:2611.21003.name: K2-Horizon: A Frontier Fleet of Open Source Language Models
pa:2611.21003.desc: We present K2-Horizon, a fleet of six fully open language models, from a 0.9B dense model to a 375B-A23B MoE, built for general-purpose reasoning and agentic work across math and science, software engineering, deep research, office automation, and beyond. The models lead or are competitive with strong open models of their size on agentic and coding benchmarks. On the modeling side, to strengthen r
pa:2611.21003.zh: 涵蓋多種尺寸且擅長各類科學與辦公任務的開源AI家族
pa:2611.21003.why: 推出從輕量到超大型的一系列開源模型，在數學、科學與寫程式等任務上表現優異

pa:2611.19937.name: AllocFlow: End-to-End Portfolio Trading Action Generation from Raw Market Data
pa:2611.19937.desc: An end-to-end flow-matching framework generates joint portfolio allocations from raw multi-asset market histories via a cross-asset flow Transformer and a two-stage imitation and group-relative reinforcement learning procedure, improving risk-adjusted returns on cryptocurrency perpetual futures.
pa:2611.19937.zh: 直接用原始市場數據來自動分配投資組合的AI
pa:2611.19937.why: 能從龐大加密貨幣市場歷史中直接產生買賣策略，有效提升投資報酬率並降低風險

pa:2611.20254.name: VoxMel TTS Technical Report
pa:2611.20254.desc: VoxMel is a tokenizer-free autoregressive TTS framework that uses an invertible two-axis Haar transform to decompose mel spectrograms into Coarse-Mel and residual tiers, enabling stable high-fidelity generation with strong recognition and speaker-similarity results.

pa:2611.17834.name: PaperCritic: Training AI Reviewers to Assess the Soundness of Papers
pa:2611.17834.desc: An AI reviewer trained by reinforcement learning to jointly maximize precision and recall of soundness review points outperforms frontier models and other training methods and transfers to other review domains.

pa:2611.21605.name: ViRA: Toward Ultra-High-Resolution Visual Agents via Cross-Input Relative Policy Optimization
pa:2611.21605.desc: Visual agents answer questions about ultra-high-resolution photos by zooming into the relevant regions. However, existing agents often answer from common sense instead of reading the evidence. Reinforcement learning (RL) on the final answer cannot correct this, because a guess earns the same reward as reading. pa:2611.18981.name: GPBam: A Retrieval-Aware German Public Law Exam Benchmark
pa:2611.18981.desc: A new benchmark of German public-law exam cases and statutory provisions jointly scores legal retrieval and long-form opinion generation across many models, finding that retrieval yields limited gains and essay quality strongly tracks prior statutory knowledge.

pa:2611.09825.name: BitDecoding-FP4: Native FP4 KV Cache Decoding via Algorithm-System Co-Design
pa:2611.09825.desc: BitDecoding-FP4 co-designs FP4 quantization and system optimizations to enable accurate, high-throughput long-context KV decoding for LLMs.

pa:2611.14960.name: Termination Lag: Coding Agents Solve Early but Stop Late
pa:2611.14960.desc: Coding agents often find correct patches early but continue working, sometimes undoing correct solutions, with termination lag varying by model and benchmark.

pa:2611.19771.name: JEPA4R: Embodied JEPA World Models with 4D Point Planning
pa:2611.19771.desc: Joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA) world models predict future embeddings instead of pixels and plan in latent space. Two challenges remain: 2D images leave the metric geometry that manipulation acts on implicit and entangled with appearance, and what these models imagine stays hidden, as they are mostly judged in simulation by short-horizon latent planning. pa:2611.06238.desc: Decision models read a document and return a probability for each of a fixed set of options instead of generating text. Several appeared in 2026, but none has published results outside English. pa:2611.21479.name: LynnReal-Hand: Unlocking World Interaction with Hand Control
pa:2611.21479.desc: Interactive video world models enable exploration through text and camera controls, yet direct object interaction requires finer control. Hands provide a natural interface, but translating continuous hand movements into coherent visual responses remains challenging because of complex hand-object dynamics and demanding real-time computation. pa:2611.11657.desc: A hybrid multi-agent trading system combining large language model analysts with momentum-based portfolio construction and rule-based execution produced a 34.5% paper-account return from March 11 to August 28, 2026, exceeding SPY's 14.4% but with a larger maximum drawdown.

pa:2611.04395.name: Correct Labels Are Not Enough: Reliable Metadata Can Silently Control Model Behavior
pa:2611.04395.desc: Fine-tuning data can include metadata that predicts the correct answer, such as a reward-model score or a quality label. We ask whether a model learns to rely on this metadata even when every training label is correct. pa:2611.08977.name: Energy-Based Reasoners: Your Recurrent Reasoner Should Be an Energy-Based Model
pa:2611.08977.desc: Energy-Based Reasoners guide looped latent reasoning by learning an energy function whose gradient refines states and signals when to stop, with exploration-based training improving performance and efficiency.

pa:2611.21412.name: Flexible Multi-Stack Super-Resolution of Clinical Brain MRI Using Hetero-Orientation Variational Encoding: Expert Reader Evaluation in a Nigerian Cohort
pa:2611.21412.desc: MS-HVED enables flexible super-resolution of partially overlapping brain MRI stacks by fusing independently encoded multi-scale Gaussian posteriors with a field-of-view-aware Product-of-Gaussians and physics-informed domain randomisation, improving reconstruction, tissue segmentation, and external clinical generalisation.

pa:2611.17610.name: More Agents, More Samples, or More Thinking? Untangling Coordination, Ensembling, and Test-Time Compute in Multi-Agent LLMs
pa:2611.17610.desc: Evaluations of multi-agent language models often compare communicating architectures against a single greedy pass. This practice confounds coordination with sample multiplicity and inference compute. pa:2611.18330.name: Marimba: A System One Model for Speech
pa:2611.18330.desc: Marimba uses frozen Qwen3-ASR features and lightweight readouts to make lexical, turn-end, language, speaker-change, and personal-information decisions from speech, achieving strong detection and calibration on conversational and read-speech benchmarks.

pa:2611.20595.name: Invariant-Aware Harness Enforcement to Protect LLM Agents from Silent API Failures
pa:2611.20595.desc: LLM agents answer questions by calling APIs and trusting the results. An API can fail silently. It ignores part of a request, such as a misnamed filter, yet returns HTTP 200 and a plausible but wrong result. pa:2611.16694.name: When Expert Disagreement Hurts: Prestige and Selectivity in LLM Decision Revision
pa:2611.16694.desc: A controlled two-pass audit varying only the revision context reveals that language models often fail to selectively correct errors under disagreement, with expert labels increasing reversals but not reliably improving accuracy, so revision should be assessed using paired conditional metrics per model and protocol.

pa:2611.08922.desc: Glyph uses foundation models and sparse autoencoders to extract interpretable clinical concepts from multimodal records and CT data, revealing reproducible predictive associations across patient cohorts.

pa:2611.17621.name: AscendGYM: A Cost-Aware Kernel Optimization Benchmark for Real-World Workloads on Ascend NPUs
pa:2611.17621.desc: AscendGYM provides a benchmark for assessing kernel optimization capabilities on Ascend NPUs using real-workload test cases, two evaluation modes, and a Speedup-Token Score that balances speedup against token cost.

pa:2611.22115.name: TeleChat to Xing4: Advancing Frontier Agentic Models on Domestic Chips and Frameworks
pa:2611.22115.desc: We present Xing 4, a series of large language models that extends the TeleChat lineage through coordinated advances in model architecture and training infrastructure on Ascend. pa:2611.22115.zh: 國產晶片與開源架構結合的全新智慧助理模型

pa:2611.23226.name: FastFrames: Video Generation at Interactive Latency
pa:2611.23226.desc: Autoregressive video diffusion models generate frames based on new observations and inputs, making them a promising medium for interactive visual experiences. pa:2611.23219.name: Do LLM Agents Still Need to Be Told How to Self-Improve?
pa:2611.23219.desc: Capable frozen LLM agents can autonomously construct context-based self-learning algorithms from basic resources and a general goal, yielding text artifacts that transfer to new game and 3D navigation tasks.

pa:2611.23143.name: TCP4D: A Unified Tool-Center-Point Tracking and Generation Model for Robot Manipulation
pa:2611.23143.desc: Robot manipulation videos provide a rich visual experience, yet recovering robot action and gripper-state annotations from RGB observations still remains challenging. Using the embodiment-agnostic tool-center-point (TCP) pose as the action space, we present TCP4D, a unified model in which a shared 4D scene representation both tracks observed TCP motion and generates future TCP trajectories. pa:2611.22275.name: Heave-Ho: Decentralized Long-Horizon Multi-Humanoid Collaboration
pa:2611.22275.desc: A decentralized framework enables teams of humanoids to coordinate whole-body loco-manipulation over long horizons using low-level multi-agent post-training and a high-level vision-language planner with speech-based leader-follower synchronization.

pa:2611.23144.name: π^4: A Foundation Model for 4D Scene Geometry and Motion
pa:2611.23144.desc: This unified foundation model enables the recovery of dense geometry, camera poses, and object tracking from diverse, uncalibrated observations in 4D scenes using a shared geometry and motion branch architecture.

pa:2611.19244.name: Agentic On-Policy Distillation Implicitly Reshapes LLMs' ReAct Patterns
pa:2611.19244.desc: On-policy distillation can improve or degrade language-model agent interaction across domains, and selectively retaining teacher-preferred positions mitigates negative transfer at a cost to source-domain learning.

pa:2611.12069.name: MPEG-Diffusion: Mixed-Resolution Video Generation
pa:2611.12069.desc: MPEG-Diffusion reduces the computational cost of video diffusion transformers by generating only a self-selected high-resolution region with dual-resolution attention and a mixed-resolution decoder, achieving faster denoising without quality loss.

pa:2611.18856.name: Self-Improvement Memory Enables Continual Recursive Self-Improvement
pa:2611.18856.desc: Continual recursive self-improvement lets harness optimizers reuse and revise prior edits across changing benchmarks or policy models by storing rationales, predicted and observed outcomes, and evaluation contexts in a self-improvement memory, improving final scores over continuation baselines.

pa:2611.21791.name: Regularized Score Centering
pa:2611.21791.desc: Asynchronous reinforcement learning increases training throughput, but data from stale policies and numerical mismatch between training and inference can destabilize learning. pa:2611.19559.name: ResWAM: Learning What Changes, Not What Stays, for World-Action Models
pa:2611.19559.desc: ResWAM combines visual residual learning in frozen DINOv3 features with a lightweight dual-branch DiT trained via conditional flow matching to improve vision-language-action policy success while lowering training and inference compute.

pa:2611.15348.name: Breath-Dx: A Time Series Classification Benchmark for Disease Screening with eNose
pa:2611.15348.desc: A comprehensive benchmark evaluates time-series classification methods on a large clinical breath dataset under realistic temporal splits, showing that sensor drift lowers performance and recurrent models are most consistent across diseases.

pa:2611.22055.name: Weight-Space Programming Doesn't Need Transformers
pa:2611.22055.desc: When large language models write neural network weights without gradient-based training, they tend to design sparse table or associative-memory models that outperform same-sized Transformers with far fewer parameters and faster GPU inference, though pretrained LLMs remain more accurate.

pa:2611.20992.name: MedJev: A System One Vision-Language Decision Model for Fast and Effective Medical Image Understanding

pa:2611.17048.desc: AURA 2.0 is a streaming video large language model that can initiate conversations, call tools, and perform interactive visual grounding, with long-horizon memory and a three-stage training scheme for improved streaming interaction.

pa:2611.21392.desc: VideoNexus separates detailed video perception from evidence-driven planning and reasoning, using perception sub-agents to return compact temporally grounded evidence and achieving higher accuracy at lower cost on long-video benchmarks.

pa:2611.23034.name: M3OPD-Reasoner: An Open Recipe for Post-Training Multimodal Reasoning with Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation
pa:2611.23034.desc: Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation (MOPD) enables a single student to absorb the skills of several domain teachers by learning from its own generated responses. pa:2611.23026.name: TPHC: Improving Hyper-Connections with Tensor-Parallel Grouped Updates
pa:2611.23026.desc: TPHC combines tensor-parallel shards with hyper-connection residual streams to enable more independent stream updates, improving language model loss and zero-shot reasoning with modest training overhead.

pa:2611.21152.name: From Repositories to Training Environments: Scaling Long-Horizon Coding Agents with Environment Evolution Loop
pa:2611.21152.desc: RepoFactory converts real repositories into verifiable coding environments and optimizes them via an Environment Evolution Loop using proxy feedback, enabling trained coding agents to achieve strong gains on long-horizon coding and agentic benchmarks.

pa:2611.23108.name: FMT: Lossless Image Compression in a Fixed Number of Parallel Steps
pa:2611.23108.desc: The Fixed-step Multiscale Tree (FMT) format achieves highly efficient, fixed-time decoding of images by utilizing a coarse-to-fine tree structure and parallel GPU prediction mechanisms.

pa:2611.23140.desc: GameRealm is a large-scale multimodal gameplay dataset with synchronized depth, camera, audio, control, and 3D trajectory annotations that improves visual foundation models for generation and geometric learning.

pa:2611.21925.name: DNeo: Your Parallel Draft Model Needs Better Target Feature Encoding
pa:2611.21925.desc: A lightweight feature-encoding method with rejection memory and architectural enhancements enables faster large language model inference by improving speculative-diffusion draft verification.

pa:2611.21938.name: HubEgo-100K: In-the-Wild Egocentric Video of Skilled Work for Robot Learning
pa:2611.21938.desc: Robot policies trained by imitation generalize poorly outside the environments and objects seen in training. pa:2611.22563.name: CADMAGEDDON: High-Fidelity CAD Reconstruction with Local Inference
pa:2611.22563.desc: CADMAGEDDON is an open-source agent that reconstructs editable CAD from meshes locally on single-GPU systems and laptops, using a mid-sized Qwen model and geometric tools to outperform prior systems.

pa:2611.22565.name: MillBill: A Machining Agent with Geometric Feedback
pa:2611.22565.desc: Turning a CAD model into a machining program requires both process knowledge and geometric precision. Language models can generate such workflows by writing geometry and toolpath code for each part, but this makes numerical execution part of the model's task. pa:2611.20995.desc: In structured Bayesian models, a large latent block is often Gaussian conditional on a smaller set of parameters, yet generic inference methods relearn this geometry during warmup. pa:2611.20003.desc: In 2025 alone, 48 new large language model (LLM) architectures were added to the Hugging Face transformers library, and many of them arrive with a technical report that presents the model as new. pa:2611.18553.desc: The WEIGHTBENCH benchmark evaluates the capacity of large language models to perform Weight-Space Programming tasks, which involve reading, modifying, and generating the weights of various neural network architectures.

pa:2611.20321.desc: A simple monocular pose estimator trained on synthetic spacecraft images shows poor real-world transfer, with overconfident pose errors and uneven gains from backbone adaptation and photometric augmentation under different lighting.

pa:2611.24669.desc: Adapting a film into a game requires selecting source elements and translating them into player actions, rules, and feedback. pa:2611.24941.name: UltraTex: Aligning Physical Knowledge for High-Fidelity PBR Texture Generation
pa:2611.24941.desc: UltraTex employs a cascaded multi-view framework that integrates physical knowledge and vision-language model features to accurately generate physically plausible PBR texture maps.

pa:2611.24362.name: PIPETTE: Prompt Injection Purple-Teaming for Robust LLM Agents
pa:2611.24362.desc: A novel framework addresses the limitations of current reinforcement learning-based red-teaming methods by employing dictionary learning and on-policy adversarial training to improve the robustness of LLM agents against indirect prompt injection attacks.

pa:2611.24869.name: WorldRuler: Interactive World Modeling under Configurable Rules
pa:2611.24869.desc: A rule-graph-based generative world model preserves user-defined rules and world states across saving and loading while accurately realizing rule-induced visual changes on designated objects and attributes.

pa:2611.22790.name: NexSight: Verifiable Tasks for Fine-Grained Agentic Long-Video Understanding
pa:2611.22790.desc: Fine-grained questions about long videos ask how many times an action occurs, in what order events unfold, or exactly when a state changes. pa:2611.23808.name: PReMind: When Personal Memory Meets Visual Hazards
pa:2611.23808.desc: A diagnostic benchmark and two-phase reinforcement learning framework enable personalized vision-language assistants to jointly connect visual hazard evidence with personal memory for appropriate responses.

pa:2611.24576.name: Late Entry in Looped Language Models
pa:2611.24576.desc: Looped language models deepen reasoning at a compact parameter count by iterating a shared layer stack T times per token, turning recurrence depth directly into sequential decoding latency. pa:2611.24098.name: RoughCut-Bench: A Benchmark for Automatic Video Rough-Cut with Large Vision-Language Models
pa:2611.24098.desc: A new benchmark and agentic workflows assess vision-language models for automatic video rough-cut, revealing current models struggle to match expert cut plans.

pa:2607.21179.name: Out of Sight, Still in Mind: Token Compression for Omni-LLMs
pa:2607.21179.desc: ReMo, a training-free method, reduces inference input token cost for omni-modal large language models by compressing redundant visual tokens through cross-modal alignment and replacing object-level visual tokens with compact text descriptions, achieving comparable accuracy on audio-visual tasks.

pa:2611.24681.name: DrawScore: Evaluating Generated CAD Models against Engineering Drawings
pa:2611.24681.desc: A new metric for automatic CAD generation evaluates models through engineering-drawing projections with a saturating penalty along curves, exposing small local errors that volume- or surface-based metrics miss and enabling use as a reinforcement learning reward or test-time verifier.

pa:2611.23824.name: Evidence-Based Credit Assignment for Search-Augmented Language Models
pa:2611.23824.desc: Reinforcement learning from terminal answer rewards enables search-augmented language models to interleave reasoning and retrieval without step-level annotations, yet outcome supervision assigns identical credit to every search in a trajectory regardless of whether it retrieved useful information. pa:2611.24830.name: A Foundation Model to Measure and Predict Human Behaviour
pa:2611.24830.desc: A foundation model fine-tuned from a large language model measures and predicts human behaviour and aligns simulated population responses with human statistics, improving accuracy over frontier LLMs.

pa:2611.24733.name: Mechanistic Critics for Sample-Efficient NPU Design-Space Exploration
pa:2611.24733.desc: NPU design-space exploration for LLM inference mainly relies on an expensive simulator that often returns only scalar feedback such as latency and power. pa:2611.14848.name: Tideway: Phase-Aware Tiered Memory Management for MoE Inference on Consumer Devices
pa:2611.14848.desc: TIDEWAY enables efficient inference of large Mixture-of-Experts models on memory-constrained consumer devices by treating host RAM and GPU VRAM as a unified memory pool with phase-aware layouts and optimized CUDA Graph execution under expert paging.

pa:2611.24738.name: Jeveration: System One Models Now Generate
pa:2611.24738.desc: Jeveration repurposes a frozen vision-language model to generate coherent images and perform image-to-image and dense prediction tasks in a single forward pass with fast 512x512 generation.

pa:2611.21114.desc: Visible artifacts are an unreliable cue for detecting generated videos, because newer generators learn to remove them. We instead detect a trace left by the generation pipeline itself. pa:2611.24154.name: Game2Player: Scaling Gameplay Experience for Visual Agents through Environment-Player Co-Development
pa:2611.24154.desc: Games are a rich testbed for visual agents, demanding perception, long-horizon planning, and precise control. However, collecting human gameplay is costly, and learning from gameplay videos requires inferring missing actions. pa:2611.19200.name: LogT: Logically Think with Images for Visual Search
pa:2611.19200.desc: Thinking with images empowers vision-language models (VLMs) to use an external Zoom-in tool for fine-grained visual search. pa:2611.22033.desc: Across three shopping benchmarks, increasing large language model shopping agents' thinking effort did not statistically improve product-choice quality but significantly raised reported confidence, and most models were poorly calibrated with correlated errors.

pa:2611.22925.desc: Visual proxies decouple explicit world-state simulation from photorealistic video synthesis, offering a controllable interface for both offline clip creation and real-time interactive streaming. pa:2611.22668.name: Let Samples Sing in Chorus: Mitigating Spurious Correlations via Cross-view Consensus
pa:2611.22668.desc: A multi-view debiasing method aggregates within-class partitions across diverse representation spaces to reduce reliance on spurious correlations and improve worst-group accuracy without bias supervision.

pa:2611.11318.name: PROLA: Principal-Orthogonal Low-rank Adaptation for Predictive Spatiotemporal Weather Downscaling
pa:2611.11318.desc: High-resolution weather prediction is important for resolving local atmospheric patterns missed by coarse global forecasts. Large pretrained weather backbones have improved global forecasting, but adapting them to produce future high-resolution fields from recent coarse states remains challenging and costly. pa:2611.23068.name: The Resolution Hypothesis: Agent Evolution's Key Is Identifying Improvements
pa:2611.23068.desc: Agent evolution is often bottlenecked by noisy evaluations that cannot reliably identify better candidate artifacts or rank methods, so progress requires making true improvements detectable and accumulable.

pa:2611.21366.name: ALIVE: Making Streaming Video Models Interactive
pa:2611.21366.desc: Streaming video LLMs can continuously observe the world, yet often handle user requests in isolation. pa:2611.17767.name: Learning Anisotropic Prediction Targets for Flow Models
pa:2611.17767.desc: AnisoFlow learns an anisotropic, learnable prediction target for flow-based generative models, improving FID and image quality without altering the architecture or sampler.

pa:2611.22287.name: Decoding Without a Decoder: Direct Pixel Prediction from Diffusion Transformers
pa:2611.22287.desc: A method that removes the decoder from latent diffusion models by adding a final-step prediction head to a finetuned diffusion transformer, reducing inference cost and improving pixel quality in image and video generation.

pa:2611.24075.name: Recurrent Domain Incremental Adaptation of Time-Series Foundation Models
pa:2611.24075.desc: PACT adapts a pretrained time-series foundation model to new operating conditions by partitioning its frozen embedding space into local charts and learning gated residual transports that preserve previously learned conditions, achieving high macro-F1 with limited labeled calibration data and no condition identity at test time.

pa:2611.24102.name: IDEA: Intent-Dominance Evidence Audit for Inference-Time Backdoor Detection in GUI Agents
pa:2611.24102.desc: A step-level inference-time audit detects visual-trigger backdoors in open-weight GUI agents by comparing instruction- and region-induced shifts in decision state against clean-step conformal baselines, localizing triggers with controlled false positives.

pa:2611.23388.name: QDA: Closed-Loop LLM Quantization Design with Agents
pa:2611.23388.desc: Post-training quantization is the standard way to serve large language models at low cost. However, the best quantization recipe differs across models and precisions. pa:2611.23994.desc: Generative novel view synthesis (NVS) employs a diffusion model to render a static or dynamic scene from a target camera view. pa:2611.24408.desc: StrideWorld is a benchmark that fixes references before motion to detect scene deformation and action inconsistency in interactive video world models, showing that most models deform scenes and only depth-scaled command models preserve composed routes.

pa:2611.24161.name: AVTR: Adaptive Multimodal Reasoning with Visual Imagination
pa:2611.24161.desc: Adaptive Visual-Textual Reasoning combines generative visual reflection with textual reasoning and learns to route between them per input, improving multimodal task accuracy while reducing inference latency.

pa:2611.17600.name: LightTAR: Light and Fast Target-Aware Representations for Multimodal Tabular Learning
pa:2611.17600.desc: LightTAR adapts dimensionality reduction to the prediction task by adding target-aware features from encoder layers via regularized partial least squares, improving multimodal tabular model performance with minimal runtime overhead.

pa:2611.23499.name: BiCAT: Bimanual Coordination Action Tokenization
pa:2611.23499.desc: BiCAT shares a motion representation across arms and conditions each arm's tokens on its partner via symmetric cross-arm attention and a joint decoder, enabling parallel arm token prediction and improving bimanual manipulation success.

pa:2611.23236.name: PGPO: Prototype-Guided Progressive Obfuscation for Privacy-Preserving LLM-Enhanced Recommendation
pa:2611.23236.desc: A prototype-guided progressive obfuscation method preserves relative item relations while perturbing high-influence semantic embeddings to defend against inversion attacks in LLM-enhanced recommender systems.

pa:2611.23751.name: Thinking Fast, Anywhere: One System-1 for the Decision Points of Any Agent Workflow
pa:2611.23751.desc: AnyS1 converts procedural skills into shared decision points, trains a small calibrated pointer model to resolve routine choices, and falls back to a large model when uncertain, reducing cost and latency while preserving reliability.

pa:2611.24654.name: CurvDelta: Low-Curvature Delta Modeling For Surgical Learning and Unlearning
pa:2611.24654.desc: CurvDelta and CurvLoRA constrain LLM updates to a low-curvature preservation space, improving retention while maintaining target adaptation across reasoning, code, and unlearning tasks.

pa:2611.23386.name: Chorus: Shared N-gram Embeddings with Layer-wise Adaptation
pa:2611.23386.desc: Chorus shares one set of n-gram embedding tables across all layers, letting each layer project and rescale the embedding using its hidden state, achieving better quality with much smaller tables and lower optimizer memory.

pa:2611.24789.name: HINT-WAM: Hindsight-Informed Training for World Action Models
pa:2611.24789.desc: World action models (WAMs) have shown promising generalization and data efficiency in robot manipulation by coupling action generation with predictions of future visual dynamics. Translating these capabilities into reliable task execution, however, remains a challenge for existing post-training methods. Offline supervised fine-tuning provides dense supervision on expert trajectories, but its flow-

pa:2611.24651.name: Piccolo: Co-Evolving Decision Models and Data through Recursive Self-Improvement
pa:2611.24651.desc: We present Piccolo, a family of multimodal decision models (0.8B to 27B) that coevolves model capabilities and training data via Agentic Data Engineering and recursive self-improvement (RSI). The models predict probabilities over candidate answers for general-purpose text and visual judgments, agent harnesses, data workflows, and interactive games. Piccolo-27B tops the Decision Index Vision Full l

pa:2611.22673.name: FVScore: Specification-Driven Neuro-Symbolic Video Evaluation
pa:2611.22673.desc: FVSCORE is a neuro-symbolic evaluation framework that compiles videos into prompt and implicit constraint propositions, verifies them with perceptual tools and soft temporal logic, and calibrates significant violations to produce interpretable, human-aligned feedback for video generation.

pa:2611.23779.name: TabBioMed: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Biomedical Tabular Learning
pa:2611.23779.desc: A large-scale benchmark of 94 curated biomedical tabular datasets standardizes evaluation across classification, regression, and multi-target tasks and finds that foundation models lead overall while tree-based models and tuned multilayer perceptrons remain competitive under cost constraints.

pa:2611.22382.name: RICoT: Recurrent Interleaved Chain-of-Thought for Page Stream Segmentation
pa:2611.22382.desc: Large language models (LLMs) have renewed interest in Page Stream Segmentation (PSS), splitting a multi-page file into its constituent documents. Yet published LLM methods still frame the task as boundary classification over one or a few neighboring pages, and commercial document-splitting APIs do not disclose their methods. We reimagine PSS for LLMs as a sequential process over the whole stream a

pa:2611.21553.name: BLIP-Live: Balancing Timeliness & Firing Precision in Proactive Streaming Video Agents
pa:2611.21553.desc: BLIP-Live unifies data, metrics, inference, and training for proactive streaming video understanding, using the PAUC-F metric and achieving state-of-the-art results on proactive streaming benchmarks.

pa:2611.16933.name: Kezek: Splitting Mono Two-Person Conversations into Per-Speaker Tracks for Full-Duplex Dialogue Data
pa:2611.16933.desc: Kezek separates a mono two-speaker conversation into per-speaker tracks while preserving timing and short replies, using a phase-insensitive speaker-fingerprint-guided two-voice activity model followed by a conditioned time-domain separator, and it improves short-reply retention, leakage, channel-swap, and runtime metrics over an open baseline.

pa:2611.24844.name: General progress substitutes for specific training data in language models
pa:2611.24844.desc: Withholding training data delays but does not prevent language models from acquiring skills, and models can regain withheld capabilities with less data as they improve.

pa:2611.24059.name: Replay, Don't Resample: Off-Policy Consolidation of Long-Horizon RL Experts
pa:2611.24059.desc: Frontier post-training follows a common recipe: train one expert per domain with reinforcement learning (RL), then consolidate the experts into one model via multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD). pa:2611.24917.name: Unified Law for Visual Tasks (The Four Laws of Computer Vision)
pa:2611.24917.desc: A unified framework, World Snapshot Models, is proposed to train and perform nearly all visual tasks by reformulating them as generation tasks, validated across over 1,000 visual tasks.

pa:2611.17605.name: Choosing Quantized Code LLMs by File Size and Energy per Solved Task
pa:2611.17605.desc: A developer running a code assistant on a laptop downloads one model file, and local inference moves the energy of every request onto that machine. A common rule says a larger model at lower precision tends to beat a smaller one at higher precision. We ran 24 GGUF files of Qwen2.5-Coder at four sizes on a fanless MacBook Air M2 and priced each in energy per solved task on 542 EvalPlus tasks. The r

pa:2611.26444.name: Mind2Act World: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Embodied Mind, Physical Action, and Mind-Action Composition in Robotic Manipulation
pa:2611.26444.desc: A diagnostic benchmark of 180 simulated manipulation configurations evaluates whether embodied systems can combine history-based reasoning, precise execution, and closed-loop environmental feedback, revealing that single-view competence does not transfer to composed tasks.

pa:2611.00911.name: S1CogBench: What System One Decision Models Can and Cannot Do on Cognitive Experiments
pa:2611.00911.desc: S1CogBench evaluates System One decision models on 24 cognitive tasks, revealing that fast decisions often lack evidence-based reasoning and vary widely in reliability.

pa:2611.25980.name: Learning What Actions Change: Action Effect Matching for Dynamics-Faithful World Models
pa:2611.25980.desc: AFFECT, an auxiliary objective that trains world models to match visual responses to temporally correlated action noise, improves rollout fidelity and planning success in simulated and real robotic tasks.

pa:2611.20455.name: Embeddings vs. Grep: Rethinking the Dense Advantage in Code Search
pa:2611.20455.desc: Code-search benchmarks show dense encoders well ahead of BM25, yet coding agents do well with grep. What does this dense advantage measure? Existing benchmarks cannot tell: they use curated queries, old code and a handicapped BM25. To find out, we build Repo-Premium, a realistic repository-level code-search benchmark. It ranks files in real repositories, with curated and raw queries in Python, Jav

pa:2611.26414.name: ZeroVLN: Learning to Navigate without Supervised Fine-Tuning of the VLM Brain
pa:2611.26414.desc: ZeroVLN is a slow-fast vision-language navigation framework that avoids navigation-domain supervised fine-tuning of the VLM brain by using a semantic tool-calling interface and closed-loop reinforcement learning to coordinate a language-based brain with an action expert, improving VLN-CE performance while preserving general visual capabilities.

pa:2611.26298.name: DailySafe: Benchmarking Dynamic Safety Awareness in Everyday Multi-Turn Multimodal Interactions
pa:2611.26298.desc: A new benchmark, DailySafe, evaluates the ability of multimodal large language models to maintain safety and address evolving risks within complex, multi-turn, real-world interactions.

pa:2611.26629.name: Posterior Matching Distillation
pa:2611.26629.desc: Posterior Matching Distillation trains a stochastic student to match a teacher diffusion model’s full posterior via tilted mean constraints, enabling high-quality few-step image generation without auxiliary score networks.

pa:2611.26510.name: AutoMaster: Autonomous Post-Training by Making the Same Model a Better Teacher
pa:2611.26510.desc: Task success alone does not specify which behaviors post-training should reinforce. Even successful teacher trajectories can contain unsupported assumptions, unproductive repetition, or superficial verification. pa:2611.25776.name: Suppressing the Shortcut Hidden Behind the Gains of VideoLLM Fine-Tuning
pa:2611.25776.desc: VETO suppresses shortcut learning in VideoLLMs by projecting supervised fine-tuning updates onto the orthogonal complement of the text-only activation subspace, improving out-of-distribution video reasoning.

pa:2611.26624.name: PlayCraft: Designing Engaging Games from Agent Play Experience
pa:2611.26624.desc: PlayCraft uses a vision-based player agent and a crafter agent to iteratively revise games, improving player learning gains and slopes across intelligence settings.

pa:2611.24193.name: WM^MLLM: Turning MLLMs into World Models
pa:2611.24193.desc: WM^MLLM uses multimodal large language models to maintain an external panorama state with revision history, enabling persistent, editable world generation from a single image with exact revisits and local edits.

pa:2611.26603.name: Depth Pro 2: Sharp and Temporally Consistent Metric Monocular Depth
pa:2611.26603.desc: A single scalable network estimates dense metric depth for images and video at native resolution, jointly improving metric accuracy, boundary sharpness, and temporal consistency.

pa:2611.25387.name: TuringSpace: Grounding Spatial Intelligence in Action with Interactive CAPTCHAs
pa:2611.25387.desc: Humans act in the visual world by inferring the 3D layout behind a 2D view, predicting how an action changes it, and correcting themselves after seeing the result. Can multimodal large language models (MLLMs) do the same? CAPTCHAs offer a natural test, since humans solve them through this very loop, clicking and dragging on the screen and adjusting after each result. Yet existing CAPTCHA benchmark

pa:2611.26409.name: WeMM-Video: Pushing the Frontiers of Open-Source Omni-Modal Video Understanding
pa:2611.26409.desc: WeMM-Video is a family of Chinese-English bilingual omni-modal foundation models that unify text, image, audio, and video processing for joint audio-visual perception and reasoning, using hybrid thinking modes and large-scale training to achieve strong open-source video understanding results.

pa:2611.21383.name: The Mask Is Not the Object: Volumetric Supervision for 3D Gaussian Segmentation
pa:2611.21383.desc: A plug-and-play objective, VODA, groups per-pixel contributors by local depth to supervise all Gaussians in selected depth clusters, improving volumetric segmentation and enabling evaluation via Removal-3D and Removal Depth Error.

pa:2611.26380.name: EgoCaptioner: Towards Comprehensive and Fine-Grained Egocentric Video Captioning
pa:2611.26380.desc: Egocentric video captioning requires fine-grained detail and accurate timing, yet current multimodal large language models (MLLMs) often miss brief actions, confuse their order, or misinterpret the wearer's motion. pa:2611.26595.name: Coda-DaVinci: Reimagining Video Generation with Code2Video
pa:2611.26595.desc: A task-adaptive agentic framework utilizes 3D proxies, physics simulation, and multi-agent coordination to enhance the structural control, physical plausibility, and visual realism of generated videos.

pa:2611.24011.name: WAM-Policy: World Action Models with On-Policy Distillation for Quadrupedal Loco-Manipulation
pa:2611.24011.desc: Arm-free quadrupeds can perform loco-manipulation, walking on three legs while manipulating with a front leg, yet no existing policy for it follows language instructions. World action models (WAMs) have emerged as effective language-conditioned manipulation policies, but are pretrained for robot arms and sample slowly. WAM-Policy turns one WAM into a quadrupedal loco-manipulation policy via two st

pa:2611.19230.name: CompoundingKernel: Self-Improving from Zero to First
pa:2611.19230.desc: We present CompoundingKernel, a self-improving agent system that writes GPU kernels by search. As of 2026-11-11, its generated kernels rank #1 on the public L1, L2 and Quantization boards of SOL-ExecBench (NVIDIA B200). pa:2611.22666.name: VSpark: Speculative Decoding for Autoregressive Vision-Language-Action Models
pa:2611.22666.desc: VSpark accelerates autoregressive vision-language-action models by improving speculative decoding with calibrated action-noise rollouts, hidden-feature alignment, and reuse of rejected-draft continuations, achieving lossless 1.28x–2.10x speedups across multiple robot manipulation tasks.

pa:2611.21373.name: WeVisForensics: Self-Evolving Agent for Omni AI-Generated Video Detection
pa:2611.21373.desc: WeVisForensics coordinates self-evolving visual and audio forensic inspector agents under a dual-timescale reinforcement learning policy to detect generated-video artifacts with localized evidence and high accuracy.

pa:2611.24809.name: On-Policy Morphing into Hybrid Attention Models
pa:2611.24809.desc: FlashMorph2 performs on-policy layer selection and weight adaptation for hybrid attention Transformers, improving long-context benchmark scores while selecting layers efficiently across model scales.

pa:2611.23835.name: NarrowSpec: Draft Hidden Width Need Not Match the Target in Speculative Decoding
pa:2611.23835.desc: Speculative decoding is widely used to speed up generation in large language models (LLMs), with a small draft model proposing tokens that one forward pass of the target model verifies. Draft models that read the target's hidden states, such as DFlash and EAGLE-3, typically inherit the target's hidden width. We show that the draft's whole residual stream can run at half or a quarter of that width

pa:2611.17460.name: Unfinished-Bench: Measuring Rule Violations by Persistent Agents in Realistic Work Environments
pa:2611.17460.desc: AI agents are increasingly equipped with persistence toward task completion to run delegated work autonomously for long periods, under many unstated constraints from internal documents and other people's authority. pa:2611.08136.name: How Far Can Untrained Neural Networks Go in Anomaly Detection? From Tables to Pixels
pa:2611.08136.desc: Untrained neural networks with fixed random nonlinear features and Mahalanobis scoring can detect anomalies competitively on tabular and visual tasks without weight optimization or pretrained representations.

pa:2611.25179.desc: An LLM-based pipeline audits simulated manipulation success checkers by recreating disagreement scenarios and visually verifying whether observed behavior satisfies task instructions, revealing phantom successes and silent failures.

pa:2611.19499.name: Do Probing and Steering Favor the Same Directions Within and Across Language Models?
pa:2611.19499.desc: The best direction for probing a concept in a language model's hidden state is not the best direction for steering the model toward that concept, with implications for transfer and abstention.

pa:2611.26286.name: Twice-Told Critiques: Claim-Level Homogenization of Peer Review in the LLM Era
pa:2611.26286.desc: Critique overlap among peer reviews is rising, and reviews identified as LLM-generated are less distinct from each other, indicating decreasing diversity of critiques.

pa:2611.26408.name: Training Vision Models for LLM-Driven Weight-Space Programming
pa:2611.26408.desc: It has been demonstrated that, in certain settings, large language models can perform weight-space programming to directly modify the weights of neural networks. However, it is unknown how dedicated training of these networks can contribute to the successes of weight-space programming. pa:2611.25935.name: TwinD: Generalizing Deepfake Detection from Blending to Entire Face Synthesis
pa:2611.25935.desc: TwinD, trained on reconstruction and blob twins derived from real frames, detects both blending and entire-face-synthesis deepfakes, improving AUROC over prior detectors.

pa:2611.26073.name: AltRA-Test: An Alternative Annotator Test for LLM Judges Without Shared Annotators
pa:2611.26073.desc: A statistical test, AltRA-Test, determines when large language models can replace human annotators by comparing inter-annotator agreement in resampled mixed human-LLM panels, and evaluations show it often requires about 100 items and makes better replacement decisions than baselines.

pa:2611.25279.name: Accord: Universal Online Metric Localization and Dense Mapping from one Camera and an IMU
pa:2611.25279.desc: Dense metric mapping from a single camera and IMU remains challenging: visual-inertial odometry (VIO) provides metric motion but sparse geometry, whereas feed-forward depth models predict dense structure without ensuring metric scale. pa:2611.26617.name: One Prior, Two Dynamics: Repurposing Video Diffusion Transformers for Self-Supervised Latent Action Learning
pa:2611.26617.desc: O2LaF repurposes a shared pretrained video model to learn inverse and forward latent action dynamics from unlabeled videos, achieving state-of-the-art few-shot action probing and zero-shot action transfer.

pa:2611.26590.name: Probing the "Conscious" Mind: Selective Access and Global Workspace in Vision-Language Models
pa:2611.26590.desc: Vision-language models (VLMs) integrate visual and textual information, but their outputs do not reveal internal concept representations. Global workspace theory (GWT) proposes that information is selected from parallel brain processes, integrated in a shared workspace, and made available to specialised processes. pa:2611.26248.name: TwinLab-Bench: Evaluating AI Scientists in Agentic Twins of Real Labs
pa:2611.26248.desc: AI agents are increasingly expected to act as AI scientists, which requires three increasingly open abilities: carrying out a given computational workflow correctly, choosing the next measurements from a given design space, and designing their own experiments. Existing benchmarks mainly evaluate the first two abilities, in a terminal or in a closed loop that selects from predefined candidates. Eva

pa:2611.26107.name: HiUni: Harmonizing Understanding and Generation in Shared Visual Space
pa:2611.26107.desc: Unified multimodal models aim to support visual understanding and generation within a single framework. However, prevailing approaches often separate their visual representations or backbone computation to accommodate the different requirements of these two tasks, which limits the degree of unification. pa:2611.26268.name: Accelerating Mixture of Block Attention via Dynamic Routing, KV-Centric Execution and Runtime Pipelining
pa:2611.26268.desc: LightningMoBA combines dynamic routing, KV-centric ownership, and runtime pipelining to accelerate long-context attention while maintaining or improving quality.

pa:2611.25005.name: Inhabitant: An Agent Framework for Long-Horizon Human-Scene Interaction with Spatial Control and Quantitative Feedback
pa:2611.25005.desc: Inhabitant enables a language-model agent to plan and execute long-horizon human-scene interactions by specifying motions spatially, measuring deviations, and revising control, achieving high task completion on the Inhabit benchmark.
